title: [Advisory] N-able N-central: 33 Zero-Days, Cloud Taken Offline
content:
##### SEVERITY AND IMPACT:
- Successful exploitation could allow attackers to steal credentials, create rogue administrators, and execute commands as root on N-central servers, compromising managed customer environments via network-accessible management interfaces.
- **Current exploitation status**: UNKNOWN, Proof of Concept Available

##### AFFECTED PRODUCTS:
- N-able N-central
- For specific versions, please check the references.

##### VULNERABILITY DETAILS:
- **Prerequisites:** Network access to the N-central management interface; some exploit chains require authentication.
- **Impact Details:** Flaws enable anonymous credential theft, administrator creation, arbitrary file writes, directory traversal, XSS, XXE, MDM impersonation, audit tampering, and root RCE.
- **Available Mitigations:**
    - Vendor hot fix is in progress; no patch is available yet.
    - **Temporary:** Hosted N-central taken offline; on-premises customers are urged to shut down servers until further notice. Restrict management interface exposure.

##### REFERENCES:
Primary:
- Source Advisory: https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/n-able-takes-hosted-n-central-offline.html

Supporting:
- Vendor Status: https://uptime.n-able.com/ (Official N-able status update on hosted environment outage)
- Proof of Concept: https://github.com/Oracle-Security/CVEs/tree/main/0-Days/N-Central%20N-Able (Researcher disclosure with PoC exploits and technical details)
- News Coverage: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/n-able-takes-cloud-platform-offline-after-30-plus-zero-days-published/ (News coverage; site currently bot-protected)

*Timestamp of the Information: 10.11.2026, 08:59*

**Update 16.11.2026**

- **Current exploitation status**: Actively exploited, Proof of Concept Available

n-able published multiple CVEs and corresponding advisories, additional fixes are still expected to adress additional vulnerabilities     
- [CVE-2026-125883 - Multiple XXE Vulnerabilities](https://me.n-able.com/s/security-advisory/aArVy0000002ihhKAA/cve2026125883-multiple-xxe-vulnerabilities)    
- [CVE-2026-125878 - Multiple OGNL Injection vulnerabilities](https://me.n-able.com/s/security-advisory/aArVy0000002ijJKAQ/cve2026125878-multiple-ognl-injection-vulnerabilities-lead-to-rce)  
- [CVE-2026-125879 - Local privilege escalation to root via nable-writable syslog-ng config](https://me.n-able.com/s/security-advisory/aArVy0000002ikvKAA/cve2026125879-local-privilege-escalation-to-root-via-nablewritable-config)   
- [CVE-2026-125880 - Stored XSS via MMS3 patch metadata (admin context)](https://me.n-able.com/s/security-advisory/aArVy0000002imXKAQ/cve202612588-stored-xss-via-mms3-patch-metadata-admin-context)   
- [CVE-2026-125881 - Schema-hint SSRF via service import schema validation](https://me.n-able.com/s/security-advisory/aArVy0000002io9KAA/cve2026125881-schemahint-ssrf-via-service-import-schema-validation)   
- [CVE-2026-125882 - RCE via file repository upload path traversal (Credit Nate Fair, Sprocket Security)](https://me.n-able.com/s/security-advisory/aArVy0000002iplKAA/cve2026125882-rce-via-file-repository-upload-path-traversal)
- [CVE-2026-91000 - Insecure IPC Channels lead to local privilege escalation](https://me.n-able.com/s/security-advisory/aArVy0000002irNKAQ/cve202691000-insecure-ipc-channels-lead-to-local-privilege-escalation)

According to [N-able's guidance](https://me.n-able.com/s/article/How-to-upgrade-Agents-and-Probes-on-N-able-N-central-version-2026-4-HF1-and-above) Agents and Probes must be upgraded by the customer in both hosted and on-premise environments.
On-premises customers are being urged to upgrade Agents and Probes and ensure Legacy API access is disabled in the environment, if it has been previously turned on.

- Additional sources: https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hackers-exploit-n-central-flaws-to.html
summary: A critical set of vulnerabilities, collectively named Able2Shell, has been disclosed in N-able's N-central remote monitoring and management platform, with public proof-of-concept exploits. Successful exploitation can expose credentials, allow rogue administrative access, and achieve root-level command execution on affected hosted and on-premises deployments. N-able has taken hosted environments offline and urged on-premises customers to shut down servers as a precaution.
